surface_case: A classic haunted-house story: a grieving woman alone in a decaying inherited home, hearing footsteps on cracked floorboards at night, glimpsing a child's ghost at the edge of her vision, trying to survive whatever is haunting the place.
true_case: The child is not a ghost — she is the narrator herself, the part of her childhood she left behind in this house to buy the ability to forget something unbearable that happened one summer. The one-eyed bear is the anchor holding that memory. Every time she remembers more, the "second shadow" comes closer. It isn't trying to hurt her — it is trying to make her stay, because being remembered means being whole again, and being whole means she must finally know what she did that summer.
core_question: What happened the summer Mara was 8 that made her split herself and forget?
emotional_question: Can Mara accept the truth of her past and reintegrate the lost part of herself, or will she remain fractured and alone?
book1_promise: The central mystery of what happened that summer will be fully revealed, and Mara will make a concrete choice about her own wholeness.
book2_hook: The memory she recovers reveals Aunt Ilse did the same thing decades earlier — the house has done this before, to someone else, and that person never left.
reader_payoff_book1: The full answer to the haunting, emotional catharsis of Mara's reintegration or escape, and the satisfaction of a concrete ending that seeds a larger story.
